issues.legal_issue: Failure to comply with a rent-payment direction does not automatically require a tenant’s defence to be struck out.
material_facts: The eviction proceeding included a claim based on non-payment of rent, and the Rent Controller directed the tenant to pay arrears and future rent.
The tenant did not make every future payment by the date directed, and the landlords sought to have the tenant’s defence struck out.
issues.conclusion: The power to strike out a tenant’s defence is discretionary, not automatic, and is an exceptional measure that must be exercised with care. The default must warrant that measure, such as by showing deliberate, contumacious, negligent, or otherwise seriously unjustified non-compliance.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15(7) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 uses discretionary language and is directory rather than mandatory; striking out a defence is penal because it deprives the tenant of protection under Section 14. The Court relied on Miss Santosh Mehta v. Om Prakash (1980) 3 SCC 610, Kamla Devi v. Vasdev (1995) 1 SCC 356, Jain Motor Car Co. v. Swayam Prabha Jain (1996) 3 SCC 55, Aero Traders (P) Ltd. v. Ravinder Kumar Suri (2004) 8 SCC 307, and Amrit Lal v. Shiv Narain Gupta (2010) 15 SCC 510. It also noted the tenant-protective purpose of rent control legislation, including the principles discussed in Nagindas Ramdas v. Dalpatram Ichharam (1974) 1 SCC 242 and M/s Rahabhar Productions Pvt. Ltd. v. Rajendra K. Tandon (1998) 4 SCC 49.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: A landlord sought recovery of premises from a tenant under rent-control law.
predicates.tenant_failed_to_follow_rent_direction: The tenant failed to make a payment or deposit required by a rent authority’s direction.

issues.definition: When a tenant fails to follow a rent direction in a rent-control eviction proceeding, striking out the defence is discretionary rather than automatic.

issues.legal_issue: The tenant’s payments and the acknowledged excess amount did not establish a deliberate or contumacious default warranting the striking out of the defence.
material_facts: The tenant paid the arrears specified in the Rent Controller’s order on the date the order was made and paid an additional amount covering ten months of rent.
The landlord acknowledged receiving the excess amount, did not refund it, and did not adjust it against future rent.

The tenant made further rent payments, and Justice Thakur considered the total payments sufficient to cover rent due at the time the defence was struck out and for a substantial period beyond that date.
Justice Thakur considered the tenant’s conduct inconsistent with a deliberate or contumacious refusal to pay rent.
issues.conclusion: Justice Thakur would allow the appeal, set aside the orders striking out the defence, and permit the tenant to contest the eviction proceeding on its merits. He considered the excess amount received and retained by the landlord applicable to future rent.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 15(7) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, striking out a defence is an exceptional discretionary step justified only where the tenant’s failure is deliberate, contumacious, or negligent. Applying Miss Santosh Mehta v. Om Prakash (1980) 3 SCC 610 and Kamla Devi v. Vasdev (1995) 1 SCC 356, Justice Thakur held that the payments and circumstances did not show such conduct. He treated the acknowledged excess payment, in the absence of refund or another direction, as held for the tenant and applicable to future rent.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and ordered_arrears_paid and landlord_retained_acknowledged_excess and total_payments_exceeded_rent_due and not deliberate_or_contumacious_nonpayment

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: A landlord sought eviction of a tenant in a rent-control proceeding.
predicates.ordered_arrears_paid: The tenant paid the arrears required by the rent authority’s order.
predicates.landlord_retained_acknowledged_excess: The landlord acknowledged receiving more than the ordered arrears and neither refunded nor adjusted the excess.
predicates.total_payments_exceeded_rent_due: The tenant’s payments covered rent due at the relevant time and exceeded that amount.
predicates.deliberate_or_contumacious_nonpayment: The tenant deliberately or contumaciously withheld rent that was due.

issues.definition: If a tenant in a rent-control eviction proceeding pays the ordered arrears, the landlord retains acknowledged excess payments, and total payments exceed rent due without deliberate or contumacious non-payment, the defence must not be struck out.

issues.legal_issue: Repeated late payment of future rent without an acceptable explanation justified striking out the tenant’s defence, notwithstanding later payments or excess payments made toward arrears.
material_facts: The Rent Controller ordered future rent to be paid month by month by a specified date.

Justice Khehar found that the tenant paid none of the future rent by the stipulated dates during the twelve-month period considered; payments were made late, including after the landlords applied to strike out the defence.
The tenant did not deposit rent with the Rent Controller or tender it unilaterally on time, and the payments were made when the landlord sought or collected them.
Justice Khehar found no acceptable explanation for the repeated delays.
The tenant had paid extra toward arrears, later paid rent, and offered to increase the rent and pay it in advance; Justice Khehar considered those matters insufficient to cure the prior defaults.
issues.conclusion: Justice Khehar would dismiss the appeal and uphold the orders striking out the tenant’s defence. He held that the repeated, unexplained failures to meet the payment schedule showed contumacious disregard of the Rent Controller’s directions.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 15(1) and 15(7) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 make the payment schedule in the Rent Controller’s order the basis for assessing compliance. Payments made toward arrears cannot be credited to future rent, and later payments do not cure earlier violations unless there is an adequate and acceptable explanation for the delay. The discretion under Section 15(7) may be exercised where non-compliance is repeated, shows disregard of the order, or lacks justification; even a single willful, contumacious, negligent, or careless default may suffice. Justice Khehar relied on Miss Santosh Mehta v. Om Prakash (1980) 3 SCC 610, Kamla Devi v. Vasdev (1995) 1 SCC 356, Jain Motor Car Co. v. Swayam Prabha Jain (1996) 3 SCC 55, Aero Traders (P) Ltd. v. Ravinder Kumar Suri (2004) 8 SCC 307, and Amrit Lal v. Shiv Narain Gupta (2010) 15 SCC 510.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and rent_payment_schedule_set and repeated_late_future_rent_payments and no_acceptable_delay_explanation and not tenant_made_timely_unilateral_payments

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: A landlord sought eviction of a tenant in a rent-control proceeding.
predicates.rent_payment_schedule_set: A rent authority directed the tenant to pay future rent according to a specified schedule.
predicates.repeated_late_future_rent_payments: The tenant repeatedly paid future rent after the dates specified in the payment schedule.
predicates.no_acceptable_delay_explanation: The tenant provided no acceptable explanation for the late payments.
predicates.tenant_made_timely_unilateral_payments: The tenant independently paid or deposited future rent by the dates specified in the payment schedule.

issues.definition: When a tenant in a rent-control eviction proceeding repeatedly pays future rent late, offers no acceptable explanation, and makes no timely independent payments, the defence may be struck out.
